sections.title: Storage + the ENS-piggybacked auth gate
sections.key_moment: The `_requireAuthorized(node)` helper consults the EXTERNAL ENS registry — `ens.owner(node)` and `ens.isApprovedForAll(...)`. That single line inherits ENSIP-1's authorization model in its entirety: if the .eth name ever transfers, the new owner is automatically the authority here too, with no separate claim step on this contract. Replicating ENS's access list on-chain would have been wrong both for gas and for staying in sync.

sections.title: The write path — `setWalrusBlob`
sections.key_moment: Authorization is the FIRST line of `setWalrusBlob`. Every external mutator (`setWalrusBlob`, `clearWalrusBlob`) calls `_requireAuthorized(node)` before touching storage. Centralising the check in an internal function — instead of inlining the require — means a future mutator that forgets to call it stands out in a diff. The pattern is a 'guard rail by convention', not by language feature, but it's the cheapest way to make missing auth visible at code-review time.

sections.title: The clear path — `clearWalrusBlob`
sections.key_moment: `delete _pointers[node]` + an explicit zero-valued event, instead of a self-call to `setWalrusBlob(node, 0, 0, 0)`. The self-call would re-run the auth gate (cheap but redundant) and would emit a 'change' event that semantically reads 'set to zero' rather than 'cleared'. Indexers that surface history care about the difference: a deliberate clear is a different user intent from accidentally zeroing the slot.

sections.title: The read path + ERC-165 declaration
sections.key_moment: `supportsInterface` claims ONLY `type(IERC165).interfaceId` — explicitly NOT the ENS resolver interface ids (`0x3b3b57de` for `addr`, `0xbc1c58d1` for `contenthash`, etc). Advertising those would create a category confusion: a client that auto-detects 'is this an ENS resolver?' would assume `addr()` and `contenthash()` exist and start staticcalling functions that aren't here. The detection pattern for this contract is a direct staticcall to `walrusBlob(bytes32)`, not an ERC-165 round-trip.
